name: Livedoid Vasculopathy
aliases: PURPLE (Painful Purpuric Ulcers with Reticular Pattern on the Lower Extremities)

criteria.description: Recurrent, painful, punched-out ulcers on the lower extremities (ankles, feet)
Healing with ivory-white stellate scars (atrophie blanche)
Skin biopsy showing hyalinization and thrombosis of dermal vessels without primary vasculitis
Evidence of hypercoagulable state (thrombophilia markers positive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Recurrent painful lower extremity ulcers healing with atrophie blanche plus histopathological evidence of thrombotic vasculopathy (fibrin thrombi in dermal vessels, hyalinization of vessel walls) without significant perivascular inflammatory infiltrate.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Livedoid vasculopathy is a thrombotic vasculopathy, NOT a vasculitis despite the historical name. It is a disorder of cutaneous microvascular thrombosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ivory-white stellate scars (atrophie blanche) on lower legs
pathognomonic.notes: Porcelain-white, stellate scars with peripheral hyperpigmentation and telangiectasia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painful, recurrent punched-out ulcers on ankles/feet
pathognomonic.notes: Small, extremely painful ulcers; pain disproportionate to size

common.notes: Pain often disproportionate to ulcer size

rare.notes: Mononeuritis multiplex from vasa nervorum thrombosis

laboratory: Thrombophilia workup: Factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A, protein C/S deficiency, antithrombin III
Antiphospholipid antibodies (anticardiolipin, lupus anticoagulant, anti-beta2-glycoprotein I)
imaging: Doppler ultrasound to exclude venous insufficiency
genetic: Factor V Leiden mutation may be present
Prothrombin G20210A mutation may be present
other: Skin biopsy: fibrin thrombi in dermal vessels, hyalinization of vessel walls, minimal perivascular inflammation
Direct immunofluorescence: fibrin deposition in vessel walls

distinguishingFeatures: APS may have systemic thrombotic events (DVT, PE, stroke)
Venous stasis ulcers are larger, less painful, medial malleolus
Cutaneous PAN has livedo with subcutaneous nodules
PAN biopsy shows necrotizing vasculitis of medium vessels

redFlags: Rapidly expanding ulcers suggesting secondary infection or alternative diagnosis
Systemic thrombotic events suggesting antiphospholipid syndrome
Ulcer non-healing despite appropriate anticoagulation therapy
references: Micieli R, Alavi A. Treatment for Livedoid Vasculopathy: A Systematic Review. JAMA Dermatol. 2018;154(2):193-202.
Criado PR, et al. Livedoid vasculopathy: an intriguing cutaneous disease. An Bras Dermatol. 2011;86(5):961-977.
Alavi A, et al. Livedoid vasculopathy: a comprehensive review. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2022;17:111.
